name: Jibble
summary: Time and attendance tracking with facial recognition, GPS and payroll-ready timesheets.
best_for: teams that need clock-ins, overtime calculations and payroll exports for unlimited people at no cost, and can live with one admin and no approval step — for them it is genuinely free, which nothing else in this category offers
skip_if: you need timesheet approvals, groups or more than one admin, which start at €1.79 per user a month on annual billing and €2.99 monthly; also skip facial recognition without checking your local rules on biometric data, which is a legal question rather than a pricing one
honest_knock:
Free forever with unlimited users holds up: the plan a new account lands on is Free, €0, with no card. What free leaves out is now readable too, because Jibble's own plan comparison sits inside the app even though the public pricing page is gone. The biggest gaps for a payroll process are timesheet approvals, automatic break deductions and more than one admin; our hands-on test below lists everything Free leaves out and keeps.

Two things to know before you build a process on it. A new organisation starts with a 14-day trial of the paid features, so for the first two weeks nothing looks locked; the limits above only show from day 15. Set up your workflow on what Free keeps, not on what week one showed you. And the paid tiers are cheap per head but add up: timesheet approvals and groups start at €1.79 per user a month on annual billing, €2.99 if you pay monthly, so a team of 25 pays €537 a year for the step most payroll processes need first.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-25 inside a new Jibble account, signed in from the Netherlands; euros, excluding VAT) Jibble still publishes no prices on its public site — jibble.io/pricing, /plans and /upgrade-plans land on the homepage — but the account carries a full price table behind its upgrade button. Four plans, per user per month: Free, €0, 'forever', for unlimited members; Essentieel €1.79 billed annually or €2.99 monthly; Groei €3.79 annually or €4.99 monthly; Pro €6.79 annually or €9.29 monthly (plan names as our Dutch-language account shows them). Monthly billing costs 32% to 67% more than annual. A new organisation starts on Free with a 14-day trial of the paid features. We saw euros; a visitor elsewhere may be shown another currency. Earlier history: on 30 August 2026 the public pricing page had been retired, and on 2 September 2026 Jibble's partnerships team confirmed to us in writing that there is no external pricing page. Jibble states an average of 4.8 out of 5 across major review platforms and app stores on more than 20,000 verified reviews.

sessions.what: We did not stop at the marketing. On 25 September 2026 we opened a free Jibble account (organisation 'AIBM hands-on test', web browser only), clocked in and out, invited a second user, exported a timesheet and opened the upgrade screen without buying anything. Nothing was agreed with Jibble about this test. Everything below is what the product did and showed, not what the site says.
findings: The account lands on Free at €0, marked as the selected plan, with a 14-day trial of the paid features running alongside it. During those two weeks nothing is locked, so what you see in week one is more than Free keeps.

The price table exists, just not on the public site. The upgrade button opens four plans with annual and monthly prices (euros, excluding VAT, as shown from the Netherlands): Free €0; Essentieel €1.79 or €2.99; Groei €3.79 or €4.99; Pro €6.79 or €9.29 per user a month. No demo form and no sales call in between.

Jibble's own plan comparison, one click further, answers what Free excludes: no timesheet approval workflow, no automatic break deductions or custom pay periods, no smart reminders, alerts or automatic clock-out, no groups, one admin, two locations, one work schedule and one kiosk, and no attendance report, leave workflow or leave balances. Free keeps overtime calculations, face recognition, selfie, PIN and NFC clock-ins, GPS-verified clock-ins and geofences, timesheet and report exports, and the Slack, Microsoft Teams, QuickBooks Online, Xero, Deel and Zapier integrations.
Setting up the organisation requires a phone number; the form will not continue without one. The marketing opt-in on the sign-up form is ticked by default.
Clocking out in the same minute you clocked in is refused, with a message saying you cannot clock out before clocking in. Jibble records whole minutes; two minutes later it worked.
Inviting a second member took a name and an email address and went through without any prompt to pay. The member shows as pending until they accept.

The weekly timesheet export offers XLS or CSV. Our CSV arrived within seconds and carries 32 columns per member per day, including worked hours, paid and unpaid breaks, deductions, payroll hours, daily and weekly overtime and billable amounts.
We did not switch on face recognition or GPS. The comparison puts both in Free; anti-spoofing, device lock and live location tracking are Pro only.

open_questions.question: Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?
